author: skyestoury
caption: How to pack out your poop ⤵️ 🥾 SEND this to your backpacking crew so you can all be prepared this summer! Not all hiking trails and campsites have toilets, and many are in high alpine areas where you shouldn’t dig a cat hole… 🧻 This means you should be ready to pack out your waste whenever heading to the trailhead.  So how do you pack your poop out on the trail? In a wag bag! 💩 🛍️ A wag bag can be as simple as a doggy bag, or more fancy like the waste bags you can buy at gear shops (shown here), that include a double bag system with kitty litter, TP, and wet wipes.  When using your wag bag, make sure to pee first to minimize the liquid that will end up in the bag.  🧻 Put all of your used TP and wipes in the bag to pack out.  🎒 Actually pack out the full/used wag bag. This is important, some people leave them 🤢 You can put it in an outside pocket of your pack or clip it to the outside.  ⚠️ And remember, don’t go near lakes or rivers. We staged this here for a pretty background but you should never actually poop this close to a lake. 200 feet away is best.  💩 If a backcountry or trailhead toilet is closed or full to the brim, do not poop behind it. Don’t even dig a hole near by. PACK IT OUT! Yes, your poop and TP.  Have questions about using a wag bag? Ask them in the comments, we’ve pooped in so many at this point on climbs, scrambles, canyons, and backpacking trips.  #b#backpackingh#hikingtipsh#howtogranolagirl #pooping
